The variable that is measured to see the effect of the change.
Variables that are kept the same so that the test is fair.
A test in which only the independent variable is changed and all other variables are controlled.

front: How many values of the independent variable should a plan include?
back: At least five, spread across a sensible range, so a trend can be seen on a graph.
To check reliability, spot anomalous results and calculate a mean.

front: Name five hazard categories used in the laboratory.
back: Corrosive, flammable, toxic, oxidising, harmful to the environment.

front: What makes a good safety statement?
back: It names the hazard and the precaution: 'wear eye protection because the acid is corrosive'.

front: What should a written plan include?
back: Variables, named apparatus with sizes, a numbered method with quantities, range, repeats, safety and how results will be processed.

front: When is a fume cupboard needed?
back: When a toxic or irritating gas is produced or used, e.g. chlorine, sulfur dioxide, nitrogen dioxide.
